diagnostics.name: Backend verifier

items.text: The execution of Majid Adineh, a detained protester from December 2025, has been carried out. He was accused of cooperating with Israel and the United States against national security. He was arrested on the evening of January 9, 2026, in Mohammadshahr, Karaj.

Hossein Ghazian referred to the Iran International survey results where over 92% of participants expressed reluctance toward marriage or having children. He noted that concern and uncertainty about the future is a significant point in the survey. This issue has also appeared in previous reputable surveys.

The New York Post reported that ship traffic in the Strait of Hormuz has nearly quadrupled in the past two weeks. This increase coincides with US efforts to create a safe shipping route near Omani waters.

Reza Goharzad, a journalist and political analyst, said the criticism by Kayhan newspaper of remarks by Masoud Pezeshkian and Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf, describing them as "signals of weakness and passivity to the enemy," reflects a division within the Islamic Republic over continuing confrontation or moving toward negotiations. He added that increased US pressure on China could force Beijing to pressure Tehran to return to talks.

The Esteghlal and Sepahan clubs released a joint poster for their match. The game will take place on Sunday, August 23, 2026, during the third week of the Premier League. The match has been titled "Superclasico."

Luiz Hamariren, head of the youth branch of the Swedish Christian Democratic Party, said at a gathering of Iranians in Stockholm that the party demands the closure of the Islamic Republic's embassy in Stockholm. He added that the world must act to support the Iranian people and their freedom. The gathering involved discussions and slogans about regime change.

The monthly report for Mordad 1405 highlights human rights violations in Iran. It mentions executions without fair trials, suppression of freedom of expression, violence against women, and labor rights violations. The number of violations across the country is alarming.

The price of the US dollar in Iran's open market reached 197,500 tomans, setting a new record. The British pound surpassed 269,000 tomans and the euro approached 230,000 tomans. The price of a new design gold coin reached 214 million tomans.

Elnaz Rekabi reacted to Farzaneh Fasihi's removal from the Iranian national athletics team, emphasizing freedom. Farzaneh Fasihi stated she has been under security pressures and was prevented from registering for the World Championships. Despite threats, she said she continues her efforts.

A group of Iranians living in the US held a car caravan protest in San Jose, California on Saturday, August 22. They protested against the Islamic Republic and carried Lion and Sun flags. This event was reported by Iran International.

Ismail Baqaei, spokesperson for the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, announced the visit of Asim Munir, the commander of the Pakistan Army, to Tehran on Monday. The visit aims to strengthen bilateral cooperation and support Pakistan's efforts for peace and security in the region. This move is part of Pakistan's continued peaceful initiatives.

The football teams Esteghlal and Sepahan will face each other in the third week of the Premier League on the afternoon of Sunday, 1 Shahrivar 1405, at Ghal'eh Hasan Khan Stadium. The match will be held on Sunday afternoon. A poll about the match result is available on Iran International Sports' Instagram page.

On the evening of Saturday, August 22, effigies of Benjamin Netanyahu and Donald Trump were hanged in Tehran's Enghelab Square. This symbolic act was carried out by supporters of the Islamic Republic. The purpose was to express opposition to the policies of the US and Israel.

Hossein Shanbehzadeh, a political prisoner in Evin Prison, has been sentenced to one year of imprisonment. The sentence was issued on charges of disturbing public opinion through spreading falsehoods. The new case relates to the release of an audio file from inside the prison.

A group of car voucher holders protested on Saturday, August 22, in front of Pars Khodro company's office due to not receiving their cars. This protest was reported based on videos received by Iran International. The protesters demanded the delivery of their vehicles.

Ruhollah Rahimpour stated that intensified sanctions and continued naval blockade could push the Islamic Republic into a 'life and death' situation. He emphasized that economic pressure might simultaneously lead to the risk of external conflict and a new wave of internal protests.

Ahmad Bakhshaish Ardestani said the US cannot maintain the blockade for a long time and will abandon it if it proves ineffective. He added that the blockade may harm Iran's economy but economic collapse is unlikely. Changes in the Supreme National Security Council have been made to break the blockade.

Abulfazl Salari, secretary of the Information Council of Khorasan Razavi Environmental Protection, denied images of a dinosaur-like creature in the deserts of Binalud as fake and AI-generated. He emphasized that dinosaurs went extinct millions of years ago. The spread of such images causes public confusion.

A group of citizens living abroad commemorated the birthday of Sattar Beheshti by sending videos. Sattar Beheshti was a blogger who was killed on November 4, 2012, due to his writings. The commemoration took place on August 23.

Erling Haaland, Manchester City's striker, has cut his long hair. This change happened before the match between Manchester City and Bournemouth in the Premier League. Haaland hopes to start the new Premier League season successfully with his new look.

Kamyar Malaki, a Bahá'í student of architecture at Birjand Azad University, was expelled due to his Bahá'í faith. He was barred from continuing his studies citing "lack of public qualification." This issue was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Some audiences believe that increased US sanctions will not change the behavior of the Islamic Republic and will put more pressure on people's lives. Some have called for sanctions to focus on the assets of officials and their associates abroad. These views were expressed in an interview with Baharan Azadi.

The mother of Setareh Rafiee appeared at her daughter's grave in a video shared on social media. She said she brought flowers for her daughter. Setareh Rafiee was killed on January 9, 2026, in Tehran.

Mohammad Abdozadeh, head of the Syndicate of Human Drug Industry Owners, stated that pharmacies have over 8 trillion rials in bounced checks. These checks are related to the last link in the drug supply chain. This indicates financial problems in the pharmacy sector.
Abbas Araghchi, Iran's foreign minister, described the US economic war as a repetitive film that Iran is familiar with. He called this war the usual bullying seen in US policies.

Jose Mourinho was dissatisfied with Trent Alexander-Arnold's performance in his first official game as Real Madrid coach and reacted strongly to a bad pass. Alexander-Arnold played about 10 minutes in the match, and Mourinho has requested a new right-back signing. He also intends to try Alexander-Arnold in a midfield position.

The mother of Moein Abbaspour spoke in a video about the pain of losing her son and expressed hope to convey his oppressed voice to the world. Moein Abbaspour was shot by officers near Golshahr Hospital in Karaj on the evening of January 8, 2026, and died.

Arash Azarmi stated that the dollar has surged to around 200,000 tomans. This has occurred while oil and non-oil revenues have decreased and currency return channels have been limited. Continuing this situation may lead to higher prices and increased pressure on people's livelihoods.

Oded Ayalon, former head of Mossad's counterterrorism unit, considers the chance of direct conflict between Turkey and Israel almost zero. He states that a war with Israel could jeopardize Erdogan's multi-year plan to expand Turkey's influence. In a military confrontation, Turkey has a larger army, while Israel has advantages in air force and missile defense.

Mohammad Reza Aref spoke about the increase in gasoline prices, expressing hope that any decision made will be good news. He emphasized that if people are not ready or oppose it, the decision will not be implemented. He also stated that reforms will be carried out step by step with public opinion.

Some Iran International viewers believe that US sanctions will not necessarily change the behavior of the Islamic Republic. They say the Islamic Republic has managed to pass the costs of sanctions to society and circumvent them. This issue was discussed in an interview with Mehdi Tajik.

A citizen reported in a video to Iran International that Mihan ice cream has become smaller and more expensive within a week. This report is from Sunday, the first of Shahrivar. Changes in the size and price of Mihan ice cream have been observed.

The value of the US dollar in Iran reached 200,000 tomans. The British pound surpassed 272,000 tomans and the euro approached 234,000 tomans. Additionally, the price of each new design gold coin exceeded 218 million tomans.

The head of the Economic Security Police announced the seizure of 997 Starlink satellite internet devices and their accessories in the first four months of this year. Additionally, 163 people have been arrested in connection with these devices. Fifteen vehicles have also been impounded.
A citizen sent a video showing contaminated drinking water in the piping of Somesara city. The video was provided to Iran International. The issue indicates water quality problems in the area.

The sister of the late Ahmad Khosravani shared an old message from her brother about his sports achievements. She wrote about his tragic fate, saying his share of talent and effort was only a bullet. She also criticized the Islamic Republic government, stating that talents became victims of this regime.

Naser Atabati, head of Tehran's judiciary, stated at his introduction ceremony that behaviors harming citizens' mental health will be addressed and they will not allow disruption of psychological peace. He emphasized fighting corruption and pursuing important cases. Utilizing social activists and media to promote culture of tolerance and reconciliation is also planned.

A group of retirees in Shush marched on Sunday, September 1, protesting their livelihood problems. They chanted slogans such as "Only on the streets can we get our rights." This video was published by Iran International.

Majid Ibn al-Reza, Acting Minister of Defense of the Islamic Republic, said about Donald Trump's post on Truth Social that described the Strait of Hormuz as part of US territory that Trump 'talks too much'. He also said regarding the US naval blockade and economic war against the Islamic Republic that Iran relies on Iranian youth and Iranian knowledge and will overcome these conditions.

The prosecutor of Hamedan announced the formation of 266 legal cases and the closure of 84 business units in the first five months of the current year. These actions were taken to protect public morality and address disturbances. Additionally, 775 legal warnings were issued, and some social media activists received warnings.

Babak Zanjani has opened the 'Sourint' cafe and pastry shop in West Tehran after returning to business. He has plans in various fields including an airline company and cryptocurrency. Zanjani was previously convicted of embezzlement and his death sentence was changed to imprisonment.
Iranians living in Spain gathered in Barcelona on Sunday, 23 August. They demanded European support for regime change in Iran. Videos of the gathering were sent to Iran International.

The National Iranian Oil Refining and Distribution Company stated that the use of methanol as an oxygenate in fuel is a recognized practice and not outside national standards. The company added that methanol is used to improve combustion and increase octane number. Earlier, the head of the automakers' association warned about the dangers of gasoline containing 35% methanol.

Manchester City has reached an agreement with Lille to sign Ayoub Bouaddi, the 18-year-old Moroccan midfielder. The transfer is valued at 95 million euros as a base fee with an additional 5 million euros in potential bonuses. Bouaddi has signed a contract with Manchester City until 2031.

The price of the dollar in Iran's free market surpassed 198,000 tomans, and the Imam coin reached 217 million tomans. The British pound also exceeded 270,000 tomans. This price surge occurred one day before the announcement of a new US sanctions plan.

Hossein Mohibi, spokesperson for the IRGC, stated that Iran maintains economic interactions near the US and bypasses it. He added that the US has started an economic war against Iran, which is an implicit admission of the enemy's military defeat. He also said Iran has plans to counter the economic war and there is no economic concern.

A cafe belonging to Babak Zanjani has been opened. At the same time, images of closures of cafes and ordinary businesses are being shared. Users have raised questions about favoritism and discrimination in dealing with businesses.

Iranians living in Japan held a protest against the Islamic Republic in Tokyo on Sunday, the 23rd of August. Videos of this protest were received by Iran International. The protest took place in the city of Tokyo.

Hassan Mansour, an economist, said that people and the market are concerned about the economic consequences of US pressures. He emphasized that reduced oil revenues cause difficulties in securing currency for imports. Additionally, exchange rate fluctuations are more influenced by US sanctions and pressures than by central bank policies.

The UK government announced that last month's cyberattack on a power plant did not pose a threat to the national electricity grid. The small power plant was offline for four days due to hackers linked to the Islamic Republic. Further details have not been released for security reasons.

The Iraqi government is considering a proposal to organize the types and quantities of weapons and register the locations of armed groups instead of handing over weapons. Tehran agrees with this proposal, and armed groups will suspend their activities for two years. Washington still insists on the actual delivery of weapons.

The mother of the late Mohsen Abbasi announced her ascent to Mount Damavand in a video. She honored her son during the climb and paid tribute to him. Mohsen Abbasi was killed at the age of 21 during protests in Najafabad.

Forough Kanaani said the Islamic Republic views imposing hijab as a symbol of its authority and tries to maintain this mechanism. During the war, optional hijab was used as a tool to show unity. She warned that if the Islamic Republic remains, the confrontations regarding optional hijab could become more severe.
A citizen sent a video showing a wall inscription in Mehrshahr, Karaj, written in English: "We love you Bibi." He says that conservative groups did not understand the message and did not erase it.

The head of the Veterinary Organization stated that pet shops operating without the organization's license are illegal. Current licenses are issued by unrelated unions. Pet shops are not allowed to sell food, medicine, and supplements for pets; these must be handled by veterinary pharmacies.

Matteo Salvini stated that Italy will not accept illegal migrants deported from Germany as long as German rescue ships continue transferring migrants to Italian ports. Italy has rejected about 80,000 requests to take back refugees in the past year due to full capacity. This issue was reported by Ali Hassanpour.
Atousa Jafari, a 27-year-old woman from Sanandaj, was killed by her ex-husband with knife wounds. The suspect fled the scene after the incident. The suspect has not been arrested yet.

Iranians residing in the UK gathered on Sunday, 1 Shahrivar, in Leeds. The gathering was in protest against the executions by the Islamic Republic. Videos of this protest have been sent to Iran International.

The Khatoun Bam women's football team topped Group E in the 2026-2027 AFC Women's Champions League qualifiers by defeating Al-Ittihad Jordan 3-1. With 7 points, the team qualified for the group stage. The group stage will be held from October 31 to November 7, 2026.

The UK Maritime Trade Center has declared the security threat level in the Strait of Hormuz as severe. The center reported monitoring commercial ships and pressure to change their routes by the IRGC. Commercial traffic has decreased in the area, and the risk of floating mines continues.

Mostafa Rostami called for serious enforcement of the law in universities by officials of the Ministry of Science and Ministry of Health. He said addressing violations benefits students, universities, and society. He also emphasized that leaving violations unaddressed harms the university environment.

The prosecutor of Mashhad announced the establishment of special branches in the city's prosecutor's office to handle cases related to "promoting nudity and immorality." Individuals deliberately involved in such activities will be prosecuted under specific legal articles. Judicial support for enforcers of moral codes has also been emphasized.

The dollar price has surpassed 200,000 tomans. Pezeshkian stated that the country is in a full-scale war situation. Mohsen Rezaei threatened that regional countries cooperating with the US would be targeted.

The National Security and Foreign Policy Commission approved an article allowing the Islamic Republic to charge fees for maritime, environmental, fueling, insurance, and safety services. These fees will be collected from ships authorized to pass through the Strait of Hormuz in rials or any other currency. The commission spokesperson announced this news.

Mahbubeh Shabani, a political prisoner, was transferred to ward six of Vakilabad Prison in Mashhad on the third day of her hunger strike. She has been deprived of visitation and phone communication. Shabani started the hunger strike in protest of poor prison conditions and the uncertain status of her legal case.

CNN reported that the Islamic Republic of Iran has increased pressure on women to comply with mandatory hijab while military tensions have eased. The government avoids direct street repression and instead uses ambiguous legal tools and economic pressures. Civil disobedience by women against mandatory hijab continues.

Benjamin Netanyahu's office stated that Israel is not seeking to escalate tensions with Ankara but will not accept any threats. Media reported that Azerbaijan is working behind the scenes to reduce tensions between Israel and Turkey. The former head of Mossad's counterterrorism division said the chance of direct military conflict is almost zero.

Majid Ibn al-Reza stated that during the 40-day war, the production of defense products in the Islamic Republic did not stop and even grew two to several times in some areas. He also mentioned that capabilities improved during operations and that the Islamic Republic obtained extensive intelligence and technological findings from the enemy. Ibn al-Reza described the recent war as one of the most unprecedented wars in history.

Babak Dadbakhsh, a political prisoner in Ardabil prison, started a hunger strike on September 1, 2026. He began the strike in protest of the lack of attention to his demands and legal situation. This news was reported by the HRANA news agency.

Esmaeil Saghab Esfahani, deputy head of government, spoke about the early days of the war, mentioning a government meeting discussing artificial intelligence when a potential attack was announced. Pezeshkian responded indifferently to the threat. Saghab Esfahani also highlighted the unity of government members during the war.

Sina Khalili won the gold medal at the World Junior Freestyle Wrestling Championship in Bratislava by defeating Kerimov from Azerbaijan. He had previously defeated opponents from Kyrgyzstan, Turkey, and the USA.

The United States Central Command announced that American forces have forced 70 commercial ships to change course by August 23 as part of the maritime blockade of Iran. They have also disabled three ships and inspected two others. This information was released along with an image of the USS John Finn destroyer in the Arabian Sea.

The dollar price has surpassed 200,000 tomans. Donald Trump's administration is announcing the toughest sanctions against the Islamic Republic. Mohsen Rezaei mentioned the possibility of nuclear weapon development and the continued closure of the Strait of Hormuz.
Younes Yousefzahi from Nehbandan has been held in Ardakan prison for over six months without a clear status. His situation remains uncertain. This issue was reported by Harana News Agency.

Scott Bassett, the US Treasury Secretary, will announce new sanctions against the Islamic Republic on Monday. The Trump administration is also trying to take control of the Strait of Hormuz from the Islamic Republic. The US now conducts 80% of the traffic through Hormuz via a dark route.

Esteghlal football team defeated Sepahan 2-1 in the third week of the Iranian Premier League. Yaser Asani and Esmail Gholizadeh scored for Esteghlal. Esteghlal is at the top of the table with 9 points.

Arzoo Karimi stated that even before the complete removal of preferential currency for medicine, prices of some imported medicines have multiplied and domestic medicines have increased up to 100%. Weak insurance systems and months-long debts to pharmacies, along with monopolies by quasi-governmental institutions, have directly transferred treatment costs to patients.

Roya Sabat, a Bahá'í prisoner in Adelabad prison in Shiraz, has been deprived of medical services and medical leave despite injuries to her back and neck. Her blood oxygen level dropped to 70 percent on August 7, but necessary medical actions were not taken. Prison authorities have not approved her medical leave.
A group of employees of the University of Wilayat company in Iranshahr, workers of Sahel Seyed company in Konarak, and railway line guards in Iranshahr reported their wage and insurance arrears.

Mike Johnson, Speaker of the US House of Representatives, stated that he expects the war with Iran to soon enter a new phase and for US allies to help end the war. He also said that preventing Iran from obtaining nuclear weapons has been the goal of all US administrations for the past 50 years. Johnson added that oil transit through the Strait of Hormuz continues and that Iranians cannot be trusted.
A trial session was held for a man accused of killing his mother with an honor motive in Tehran's criminal court. The session is for addressing the murder charge. The court is reviewing the case.

Javad Nekounam, head coach of Tractor, expressed his sadness over the ban on spectators and said the decision was made earlier. He emphasized that the team is playing well despite missing two top offensive players. Nekounam also stated that the team's focus is on overall league success and not on breaking records.

Siamak Mirzaei, Asghar Akbarzadeh, and Ali Vasaghi, three Turk activists, have been detained in Ardabil prison for over 57 days. They remain in judicial uncertainty, and two of them have been deprived of proper medical care. These activists are held in separate wards alongside prisoners accused of drug-related crimes.

Mohsen Rezaei threatened to build an atomic bomb. There was also discussion about a 200,000 toman dollar and a split in the leadership. This topic was raised in the audio version of Titraval with Niusha Saremi.

Sohrab Bakhtiarizadeh said after Esteghlal's victory over Sepahan that the players have the biggest share of the success. He explained the benching of Alireza Koushki and emphasized the importance of discipline for the team. He also stated that despite the closed transfer window, he believes in his players.
The 184th issue of the Peace Line monthly magazine has been published. This magazine addresses peace-related topics. The new issue is now available to readers.

A US startup in the UAE is producing affordable interceptors to counter drones from the Islamic Republic. These interceptors are 3D printed and cost about five thousand dollars each. The goal is to produce 15,000 interceptors monthly by mid-2027.

The European Union has deployed forces and helicopters to control a large fire in the Deliblatska Sand area in northeastern Serbia. The fire has been ongoing since late July and has burned thousands of hectares of forest. The situation has stabilized somewhat, but the fire is not yet fully contained.

Reza Pahlavi stated that the dollar price is now 28,571 times higher than at the start of the Islamic Republic. He described the regime as responsible for poverty, corruption, and isolation, saying reform is impossible. He also urged people to work towards weakening and removing the regime.

Morad Vaisi, a senior analyst at Iran International, stated that the market has raised the dollar price due to escalating tensions between the Islamic Republic and the US and the possibility of war. He predicted that the dollar will not stop at 200,000 tomans and there is no ceiling for its price increase. This market reaction stems from concerns about oil export cuts and reduced foreign currency revenues.
Barcelona defeated Elche 5-0 in their first La Liga match. Rafinha and Freeman Lopez each scored twice, and Karim Ademi scored one goal. Gordon provided two assists in six minutes of play.

Sepahan fans criticized the players as 'dishonorable' after their defeat against Esteghlal at Ghal'eh Hasan Khan stadium. Sepahan has won only one of their first three Premier League matches. They lost to Esteghlal and Tractor.

The Cabinet opposed the National Security Commission's report on the plan to counter foreign infiltration. The opposition was due to scientific restrictions and increased brain drain. The plan's negative national and international repercussions were also mentioned.

Mohammad Taghavi analyzed the Esteghlal vs Sepahan match, stating Sepahan played poorly in both halves and Esteghlal lost motivation after scoring two goals. He added that if Esteghlal had played like in the first half, they would have scored more goals. He also highlighted Esmaeil Gholizadeh's smart play for Esteghlal.

The Jerusalem Post reported that the war has destroyed about one million jobs, increasing unemployment and severe price hikes, putting pressure on people's daily lives. The suicide of a 35-year-old worker in Mahshahr highlights the gap between the economic situation of the people and the military structure of the Islamic Republic. Food inflation in July reached 128%, with meat and dairy prices rising over 140%.

Mohsen Rezaei spoke about the possibility of building an atomic bomb after his appointment as Secretary of the Supreme National Security Council. These remarks caused increased tension in the currency market and pushed the dollar past 200,000 tomans. The market also anticipated a tightening of the US blockade, which increased demand for foreign currency.

The Syrian foreign minister announced the possibility of resuming security talks with Israel. Despite distrust, Damascus considers diplomacy the only way to resolve tensions. He urged Tel Aviv to seize the historic opportunity for an agreement.

Emmanuel Macron described Mohammed bin Salman's visit to France as an important step in bilateral relations. He emphasized joint efforts for regional peace and stability and expanding cooperation in various fields. The visit took place amid ongoing tensions in the Middle East.

Scott Bassett warned that countries maintaining financial and trade relations with the Islamic Republic must choose between cooperating with Tehran or retaining access to the global financial system. He announced a new phase of economic pressure against the Islamic Republic, aiming for a broad attack on Iran's financial and trade resources. He also warned that if Iran takes military action against US forces or Gulf countries, there will be a swift and decisive response.

The Hawk fire near Reno in Nevada has spread over 42 square kilometers. The governor declared a state of emergency and about a thousand homes are at risk. Evacuation orders have been expanded in Washoe County.

Syria's official news agency, SANA, reported that senior Syrian and Israeli officials met in Jordan with US mediation. The talks focused on halting Israeli attacks and resuming negotiations for a security agreement. Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani also told Reuters that security negotiations are likely to resume soon.

JD Vance stated that the US exports between seven to fifteen million barrels of oil daily through the Strait of Hormuz. He said Washington is trying to prevent an energy crisis that the Islamic Republic seeks to create. Vance emphasized that the Islamic Republic cannot cut international trade routes and that the US has multiple tools to counter it.

Greece has transferred a Patriot air defense battery from Karpathos to Crete. This move follows threats from the Islamic Republic against US military bases in Europe. The Patriot system will be deployed to protect the Souda military base.

Brent crude oil prices fell by more than one percent. This price drop occurred before the announcement of a new US sanctions package against the Islamic Republic. The US Treasury Secretary announced the start of an "economic D-Day" against Iran.

The US has launched a new campaign to cut Iran's economic lifelines. Mohsen Rezaei threatened that if the economic war continues, no oil exports from the Persian Gulf will be allowed. Iran can increase global costs by restricting the passage of oil tankers.

Ibn al-Reza, the acting defense minister of the Islamic Republic, claimed that the armed forces gained significant intelligence and technological findings during the recent war. He stated that the Islamic Republic inflicted effective strikes on the enemy at a lower cost. He also said that the war experience led to a reassessment of military priorities and preparation for threats over the next 50 years.

The Islamic Republic has proposed a plan to charge commercial ships passing through the Strait of Hormuz, which has not yet been approved. This plan arises from financial pressures due to sanctions and reduced oil revenues. Its implementation could increase shipping and insurance costs and affect Tehran's relations with regional countries.

Tractor and Persepolis have faced each other many times in the past fifty years, but in recent years they have had the most conflicts and controversies. These conflicts have led to their matches being held without spectators. Discussions about this issue took place in the Hattrick program.
